\section[el valor]{el valor — courage; value}

\label{lesson:ES-C722-valor}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the fault, then the Spanish for to value.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el valor}
\textbf{el valor} — \textquotedblleft{}courage; value\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Hace falta valor para decir la verdad.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{It takes courage to tell the truth.}
\end{quote}

Two senses: courage and value (\emph{el valor de una casa}).

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{valor} comes from Late Latin \emph{valor}, \emph{valōrem} (EtymDB), from \emph{valēre} \textquotedblleft{}to be strong, to be worth\textquotedblright{}; strength and worth stayed in one word.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el valor}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el valor}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el valor}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the fault, then the Spanish for to value, then say \emph{el valor} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does el valor mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Courage; value\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[el coraje]{el coraje — guts, courage; anger}

\label{lesson:ES-C722-coraje}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to value, then the Spanish for courage.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el coraje}
\textbf{el coraje} — \textquotedblleft{}guts, courage; anger\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Tuvo el coraje de hablar.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{She had the courage to speak.}
\end{quote}

In Mexico and other countries \emph{me da coraje} means it makes me angry.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{coraje} was borrowed from Old Occitan \emph{coratge} (EtymDB), built on Latin \emph{cor} \textquotedblleft{}heart\textquotedblright{}; English \emph{courage} is the French form of the same word.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el coraje}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el coraje}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el coraje}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to value, then the Spanish for courage, then say \emph{el coraje} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does el coraje mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Guts, courage; anger\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[la valentía]{la valentía — bravery}

\label{lesson:ES-C722-valentia}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for courage, then the Spanish for guts.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la valentía}
\textbf{la valentía} — \textquotedblleft{}bravery\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Todos admiran su valentía.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Everyone admires her bravery.}
\end{quote}

Built on \emph{valiente}, brave.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{valentía} is built on \emph{valiente} \textquotedblleft{}brave\textquotedblright{}, usually explained as the old participle of \emph{valer}, from Latin \emph{valēns} \textquotedblleft{}strong\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{valēre} \textquotedblleft{}to be strong\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la valentía}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for courage, then the Spanish for guts, then say \emph{la valentía} again

\section[cobarde]{cobarde — cowardly; the coward}

\label{lesson:ES-C722-cobarde}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for guts, then the Spanish for bravery.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: cobarde}
\textbf{cobarde} — \textquotedblleft{}cowardly; the coward\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
No seas cobarde y llámala.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Do not be a coward, call her.}
\end{quote}

Same form for men and women: \emph{es una cobarde}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{cobarde} was borrowed from Old French \emph{cuard} \textquotedblleft{}coward\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), built on \emph{coue} \textquotedblleft{}tail\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{cauda}: the animal that runs with its tail down.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cobarde}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cobarde}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{cobarde}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for guts, then the Spanish for bravery, then say \emph{cobarde} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does cobarde mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Cowardly; the coward\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[atreverse]{atreverse — to dare}

\label{lesson:ES-C722-atreverse}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for bravery, then the Spanish for cowardly.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: atreverse}
\textbf{atreverse} — \textquotedblleft{}to dare\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
No me atrevo a decírselo.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I do not dare to tell him.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Atreverse a} + infinitive.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{atreverse} is inherited from Latin \emph{tribuere} \textquotedblleft{}to grant, to assign\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), used with \emph{se}: to grant oneself the right to do something.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{atreverse}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{atreverse}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for bravery, then the Spanish for cowardly, then say \emph{atreverse} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
